ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, five congruent isosceles triangles are pieced together to form two regular pentagons of different sizes, inside and outside. If the side length of the smaller regular pentagon is 1, what is the side length of the larger regular pentagon?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend CF to intersect BA at point H, \\
since assembling 5 congruent isosceles triangles forms two differently sized regular pentagon patterns, \\
therefore $\angle$BAE=$\angle$CBA=108$^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle$ABG+$\angle$BAG=108$^\circ$, \\
$\angle$ABG+$\angle$BAG+$\angle$AGB=180$^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle$AGB=$\angle$BAG=180$^\circ$−108$^\circ$=72$^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle$ABG=180$^\circ$−72$^\circ \times 2$=$36^\circ$, \\
since AB=BC, \\
therefore $\angle$BHC=(180$^\circ$−108$^\circ$)÷2=$36^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle$CBF=$\angle$CFB=108$^\circ$−36$^\circ$=72$^\circ$=$\angle$AFG, \\
therefore $\angle$FHG=180$^\circ$−72$^\circ \times 2$=36$^\circ$=$\angle$ABG, \\
therefore points A and H coincide, \\
therefore $\angle$FAG=72$^\circ$−36$^\circ$=36$^\circ$=$\angle$ABG, \\
therefore $\triangle$BAG$\sim$$\triangle$FGA, \\
therefore $\frac{BA}{AG}=\frac{AG}{FG}$ \\
Let BF=AF=AG=x, then BG=AB=x+1, \\
therefore $\frac{1+x}{x}=\frac{x}{1}$ \\
Solving it: $x_{1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$, $x_{2}=\frac{1−\sqrt{5}}{2}$ (discard since it does not meet the conditions), \\
therefore AB=1+$\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$=\boxed{\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}}.

In △ABG, the corresponding structure gives AB=BG, so ∠BAG=∠AGB; therefore ∠BAG=∠AGB=72°, and ∠ABG=36°. After further extending CF to H, using AB=BC and the 108° interior angle of the outer pentagon, ∠BHC=(180°−108°)/2=36° is obtained. Therefore ∠ABG=∠FAG=36°, and B, F, G being collinear makes ∠AGB=∠FGA=72°, so △BAG∼△FGA. The similarity ratio gives BA/AG=AG/FG. Let BF=AF=AG=x, and FG=1. Because B, F, G are collinear and F is between B and G, BG=BF+FG=x+1; the side length of the outer regular pentagon AB=BG=x+1. Substitute into the similarity proportion: (x+1)/x=x/1, namely x^2=x+1. Use the diagram to choose labels so that F lies on the same straight outer-side line segment as B and G, and the congruent isosceles-triangle sides give BF = AF = AG. Angle chase around the adjacent outer vertices and the isosceles triangles to get angles of 36 degrees and 72 degrees; specifically show that triangle BAG and triangle FGA are similar. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, five congruent isosceles triangles are pieced together to form two regular pentagons of different sizes, inside and outside. If the side length of the smaller regular pentagon is 1, what is the side length of the larger regular pentagon?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Extend CF to intersect BA at point H. Since assembling 5 congruent isosceles triangles forms two differently sized regular pentagon patterns, therefore $\angle BAE=\angle CBA=108^\circ$, therefore $\angle ABG+\angle BAG=108^\circ$, and $\angle ABG+\angle BAG+\angle AGB=180^\circ$, therefore $\angle AGB=\angle BAG=180^\circ-108^\circ=72^\circ$, therefore $\angle ABG=180^\circ-72^\circ \times 2=36^\circ$. Since $AB=BC$, therefore $\angle BHC=(180^\circ-108^\circ)\div 2=36^\circ$, therefore $\angle CBF=\angle CFB=108^\circ-36^\circ=72^\circ=\angle AFG$, therefore $\angle FHG=180^\circ-72^\circ \times 2=36^\circ=\angle ABG$, therefore points A and H coincide, therefore $\angle FAG=72^\circ-36^\circ=36^\circ=\angle ABG$, therefore $\triangle BAG\sim\triangle FGA$, therefore $\frac{BA}{AG}=\frac{AG}{FG}$. Let $BF=AF=AG=x$, then $BG=AB=x+1$, therefore $\frac{1+x}{x}=\frac{x}{1}$. Solving it: $x_1=\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$, $x_2=\frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2}$ (discard since it does not meet the conditions), therefore $AB=1+\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}=\boxed{\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a geometric figure without text labels; the outer contour is a regular pentagon, the interior is pieced together from five congruent isosceles triangles, and encloses a smaller regular pentagon. According to the method given in the problem, label the outer regular pentagon clockwise as A, B, C, D, E; take one side of the small regular pentagon as FG, and FG=1; from the adjacent line segment relationships in the figure, the labels may be chosen so that B, F, G are collinear, and from the legs of the congruent isosceles triangles, BF=AF=AG is obtained. Reasoning: Extend CF to meet BA at H. The large and small pentagons are both regular pentagons, so their interior angles are all 108°. From the adjacent vertex angle relationships of the outer pentagon, ∠BAE=∠CBA=108°, and angle chasing gives ∠ABG+∠BAG=108°. In △ABG, the corresponding structure gives AB=BG, so ∠BAG=∠AGB; therefore ∠BAG=∠AGB=72°, and ∠ABG=36°. After further extending CF to H, using AB=BC and the 108° interior angle of the outer pentagon, ∠BHC=(180°−108°)/2=36° is obtained. Continuing angle chasing gives ∠CBF=∠CFB=108°−36°=72°, and correspondingly obtains ∠AFG=72°; meanwhile ∠FHG=180°−72°×2=36°=∠ABG, therefore H coincides with A. Thus ∠FAG=72°−36°=36°. Therefore ∠ABG=∠FAG=36°, and B, F, G being collinear makes ∠AGB=∠FGA=72°, so △BAG∼△FGA. The similarity ratio gives BA/AG=AG/FG. Let BF=AF=AG=x, and FG=1. Because B, F, G are collinear and F is between B and G, BG=BF+FG=x+1; the side length of the outer regular pentagon AB=BG=x+1. Substitute into the similarity proportion: (x+1)/x=x/1, namely x^2=x+1. Solving gives x=(1+sqrt(5))/2, and the negative root is discarded. Therefore the side length of the large regular pentagon AB=x+1=(3+sqrt(5))/2.
